summary: Cataract, a Monroe County, Wisconsin tower listed by the FFLA as standing; no build date, builder, height, staffing or access rules were found.

evidence.supports: Listed by the FFLA in Monroe County as a standing tower with coordinates
Wisconsin had 119 towers at the height of their use
evidence.quote: At the height of their use, 119 towers dotted the landscape.

evidence.supports: Many surviving towers were built in the 1930s by Civilian Conservation Corps crews
evidence.quote: Many of the towers we see still standing today were built during the 1930s by the young men of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: Towers were manned from May to September for many decades
evidence.quote: Manned from May to September for many decades, their staffing was reduced to the peak forest fire season

evidence.supports: 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned in 2015
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: DNR now monitors forests for fire from the air
evidence.quote: Today, the Wisconsin DNR monitors it’s forests for fires from above by airplane

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLA line (coordinates, Tower, Standing) is confirmed for this site. The record's elevation_m 409 comes from an OpenStreetMap node, but the OSM page as fetched showed no elevation text, so it is unverified and left out of the story. A search summary gave 408 ft (1,339 m) from another listing, which I did not read. Cataract is described in search results as a place in the Town of Little Falls; that was not confirmed on a page I read, so it is not used. The WJFW article is general history and does not name Cataract, so whether Cataract was one of the 72 towers decommissioned in 2015 is unknown. No build date, builder, height, staffing, or access rules were found. The Wikipedia page for the community and Door County Pulse were not used. Greenfield and Norway Ridge are other Monroe County towers listed by the FFLA; they are not part of this record. The story is short because the evidence is thin; a Wisconsin DNR or Monroe County records check is the next step.
